edges.effect_quant: Topical minoxidil is one of the best-supported nonsurgical treatments for androgenetic alopecia, improving hair density versus placebo in both men and women.
edges.mechanism: Minoxidil appears to prolong the anagen phase, enlarge miniaturized follicles, and improve local follicular signaling in scalp tissue. The effect is supportive rather than curative, meaning benefit depends on continued use and tends to fade when treatment stops.
edges.summary: Unlike many cosmetic hair-loss products, minoxidil has a real evidence base. Successive systematic reviews and pooled trial analyses show that it outperforms placebo for hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia, even though the magnitude of visible benefit varies by concentration, sex, and adherence.
edges.caveats: The effect is gradual and maintenance-dependent, so expectations need to stay realistic. Adverse effects are usually local and mild, but the data are stronger for topical use than for newer off-label oral strategies.
